Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice and plant materials; Acacia pennata (Thembra) reported in some accounts
Equipment: Household vessels and starter cakes; exact equipment varies
Method_Description: Traditional starter preparation is described in published studies; botanical composition should be recorded per source/locality.
Variation_by_Locality: Variation must be verified; do not treat a reported plant list as universal.
Evidence_Notes: Summary of published descriptions; requires source-by-source extraction.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; Bairing and Bora rice reported
Method_Description: Rice is cooled, mixed with starter and fermented; one study reports approximately five to seven days, depending on conditions.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: About 5–7 days reported in one study; not a universal standard
Variation_by_Locality: Household, seasonal and locality variations need verification.
Evidence_Notes: Do not treat a reported duration as a universal recipe or safety validation.

Equipment: Collection equipment not fully standardised in current record
Method_Description: Liquid is collected from fermented material; fresh and preserved forms are reported.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Preservation duration and storage conditions not yet established
Variation_by_Locality: Need detailed source extraction and local confirmation.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; rice varieties vary by source and locality
Method_Description: Published sources describe cooked rice inoculated with starter and fermented; unlike Poro Apong, the cited 2023 account describes Noggin Apong without ash addition and as a liquid extracted from fermented material.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: No universal duration recorded in this archive
Variation_by_Locality: Must be checked across districts and households.
Evidence_Notes: Summary of published descriptions; no standardised universal recipe inferred.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice; ash from rice husks or bran reported
Equipment: Household fermentation vessels; full apparatus needs source-level verification
Method_Description: Published descriptions distinguish Poro Apong by adding ash from rice husks or bran to cooked rice before fermentation.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: No universal duration recorded in this archive
Variation_by_Locality: Ash material and process details require locality-specific comparison.
Evidence_Notes: Source summaries disagree or vary in detail; record each process description separately rather than assuming a standard method.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Fermented rice mixture with reported rice-husk/bran ash addition
Equipment: Distillation equipment not sufficiently documented in current sources
Method_Description: The 2023 article describes Poro/Por Apong as fermented and then distilled; further source extraction is required for equipment, sequence and variation.
Evidence_Notes: Do not confuse this form with the non-distilled Noggin Apong description.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Soaked glutinous rice and locally collected plant materials
Equipment: Pounder; drying surfaces; earthen storage container reported in one Sivasagar study
Method_Description: A 2023 field study documented ÉPOP preparation using 31 plant species across 22 families in Sivasagar district; plant materials were dried, crushed and mixed with soaked glutinous rice, formed into cakes, inoculated with prior starter material and dried for storage.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: One study reports prepared starter cakes can be stored up to six months; this is not a universal guarantee.
Variation_by_Locality: Plant lists and preparation customs vary and should be attributed to the particular village/study.
Evidence_Notes: The 31-species inventory belongs to the sampled Sivasagar study and must not be universalised to all Mising communities.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice and locally collected plant parts; ingredients differ by study and village
Starter_Culture: Mod pitha; Chuzae-pitha in a Dhemaji study
Equipment: Wooden grinder (dheki), bamboo sieving/handling implements and drying surfaces are reported in older fieldwork
Method_Description: A 2007 ethnobotanical study describes rice and dried plant materials ground together, shaped into starter cakes and inoculated/maintained using older starter material. A 2010 study records a different locality-specific Deori starter plant inventory in Dhemaji.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: Starter preparation seasons September–October and February–March are reported by a later survey for its study area only.
Variation_by_Locality: Plant lists and local starter names vary across villages and studies.
Evidence_Notes: Do not combine the 32-species 2007 inventory and the 15-species Dhemaji inventory into one universal recipe.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Rice and prepared starter cake; water is used in the documented process
Starter_Culture: Mod pitha; Chuzae-pitha in a Dhemaji study
Equipment: Earthen fermentation vessel (koloh/disoh in one older account); vessel terminology varies by source
Method_Description: Older fieldwork describes cooked or prepared rice inoculated with starter and fermented in a covered vessel; liquid is strained before serving. Exact steps differ across publications and should be transcribed source by source.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: One 2007 study reports 3–4 days in summer and about a week in winter; this is a historical, study-specific observation, not a universal process standard.
Variation_by_Locality: Season, vessel, starter and household practice need current verification.
Evidence_Notes: Do not present old fermentation durations or storage claims as food-safety guidance.

Equipment: Straining basket/utensil reported in older fieldwork
Method_Description: The fermented material is strained to obtain the beverage; a 2007 account reports seasonal differences in taste and keeping time.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: One 2007 account reports up to about one month in winter and 2–3 weeks in summer before souring; not a universal shelf-life or safety guarantee.
Variation_by_Locality: Storage conditions and current practice require field verification.
Evidence_Notes: Historical sensory and storage observations must not be treated as validated shelf-life recommendations.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Water-soaked rice and plant materials; Croton joufra (Marthu) is described as a principal ingredient in the 2006 field paper; other plants/substitutes reported in surveys
Equipment: Wooden mortar (long) and pestle (lingpum); bamboo sieve (ingkrung); sun/fire-place drying described in a historical account
Method_Description: Teron (2006) describes soaked rice and Marthu leaves being pounded, previously prepared thap being added, and the mixture shaped into flat cakes and dried. Other studies report additional plants or substitutions; keep each inventory tied to its source.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: One historical account reports 2–5 days of drying depending on conditions; not a universal specification.
Variation_by_Locality: Starter ingredients and substitutes vary across sources and localities.
Evidence_Notes: Do not merge plant inventories from different studies into one universal recipe; ethnomedicinal claims are not clinical evidence.

Ingredients_or_Materials: Cooked rice, water and powdered thap
Method_Description: Cooked rice is cooled and mixed with powdered thap; the 2012 survey describes an initial fermentation followed by additional fermentation after water is added. Teron (2006) also describes the fermented rice beverage as Hor-alank. Preserve source-specific sequences rather than combining them into a single definitive method.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: A 2012 survey reports an initial 2 days followed by 2–4 further days depending on season in its study context; not a universal process standard.
Variation_by_Locality: Season, rice, vessel and process vary and need current verification.
Evidence_Notes: Historical descriptions only; no food-safety validation is implied.

Starter_Culture: Thap is used upstream in Hor-alank fermentation
Equipment: Traditional still called Bhot in Teron (2006); improved stills also discussed
Method_Description: Hor-arak is described as the distilled form obtained from Hor-alank. The historical paper documents traditional and improved still apparatus, but the archive needs further extraction of diagrams, terminology and locality-specific differences.
Reported_Duration_or_Conditions: No single universal duration or equipment specification recorded.
Variation_by_Locality: Still design and use need locality-specific and current documentation.
Evidence_Notes: This record documents cultural/process history, not instructions for producing or consuming alcohol.
